newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore humanitarian stand on Cambodian arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Singapore humanitarian stand on Cambodian arrivals.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday its approach to the arrival of ousted Cambodian Prince Norodom Ranariddh's son and other Cambodians was based on humanitarian considerations and done with the clearance and concurrence of the Cambodian authorities.
"Singapore is even-handed about this," the spokesman from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) said in a statement replying to press queries.
"Singapore has in fact allowed relatives of both parties to the current conflict in Cambodia to enter Singapore as and when they have requested to do so", he said.
Almost a dozen members of Cambodia's royal family left the country on special flights on Wednesday, three days after the ouster of Ranariddh as first prime minister, witnesses in Phnom Penh said.
Ranariddh's sister, Princess Bopha Devi, and his son, Prince Norodom Chakravuth, were the most prominent members of the royal family to leave.
The Princess was believed to have been on a flight to Bangkok while Chakravuth left on a later flight to Singapore.

Some nine other members of the family, as well as senior officials from Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party and his cabinet, took flights out of the country to Singapore and Bangkok, the witnesses said.
